chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the man who is seized by nosebleed and vomiting during the prayer, what should he do? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should turn away, wash his nose, and return to his prayer. But if he speaks, let him repeat his prayer, and there is no (need for) ablution upon him.'

key_terms.يَنْفَتِلُ: He turns away (from the prayer position)

ai.seo_question: Does nosebleed or vomiting break wudu or invalidate the prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that minor bodily discharges like nosebleeds or vomiting do not invalidate wudu, allowing the worshipper to continue their prayer after cleaning the affected area. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between major impurity (janabah) and minor impurity (hadath), emphasizing that only speech or major impurities necessitate a full prayer repetition. The hadith underscores the practical ease (rukhas) granted to believers during worship, ensuring that natural bodily functions do not become undue burdens.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Fazalat, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the man seized by the nose-bleed and the vomiting during the Salāt, how he should react. Heasws said: ‘He should turn and wash his nose, then return to his Salāt. But if he speaks, so let him repeat his Salāt, and there would be no (repeat) ablution upon him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences nose bleeding and vomiting while in Salah (prayer). What is he to do? He (the Imam) said, ‘He turns to wash his nose and comes back to his Salah (prayer). If he has spoken, he must perform his Salah (prayer) again, but he does not need Wudu’.’”
